cards.title: Follow-ups are not a formality
cards.body: The doctor wants to know what happened since last time. Bring the evidence and the visit becomes real progress, not guesswork.

cards.title: The last prescription, the actual paper
cards.body: Not a blurry forward from the family group. The original shows exactly what was prescribed, so changes can be made on top of it.

cards.title: Every medicine currently being taken
cards.body: Strips in a bag, including any from other doctors and anything bought over the counter. This catches overlaps nobody noticed.

cards.title: Readings since the last visit
cards.body: If the doctor asked for home BP or sugar checks, bring them written with dates and times. A week of honest numbers beats one good morning.

cards.title: Tests the doctor asked for
cards.body: Reports printed or on the phone, in date order. If a test wasn't done, say so. Better than the doctor assuming it was normal.

cards.title: A short note on what changed
cards.body: Better, worse, new symptoms, missed doses, side effects. Two or three lines written at home beat memory in the room.

takeaway: Bring the last prescription, every current medicine, dated readings, requested tests and a short note on what changed.
share: Follow-up visit checklist: old prescription, all medicines, readings, reports, and a note on what changed.
